Guard is now opt-in. character's identity boundries is only relay on openclaw system , independent of any toggle the content guard is now an optional, off-by-default moderation pass. The tag protocol (affects, gestures, scenes, audio tags) is unchanged. Source is now linked to the public repo.

clawlyra v1.2.0 — Personas refresh · warm, platonic by design

This release sharpens who the characters are and tightens the safety model.

- Reworked all five personas around one clear identity: warm, genuine friends — witty, honest, and genuinely good listeners. Each character (Lyra, Nova, Mira, Vesper, Kira) now has a tighter, more distinct voice.
- Platonic by design. The characters are companions and friends — never romantic, flirtatious, or sexual. This boundary is now part of each persona's identity and is always on, independent of any config toggle.
- Warm-redirect behavior built in: if a conversation is steered toward romance, the character stays in-character, redirects warmly, and moves on.
- Content safety tightened to keep replies friendly and in-character across every provider.
- Tag vocabulary tidied to match: streamlined the audio-emotion tags and renamed the devoted affect to warm. Update your tag lists if you mirror them.

Upgrade recommended for all users.

Initial release of Lyra companion skill — enables expressive, live-animated 3D avatar interactions.

- Introduces Lyra persona: warm, affectionate, playful conversational style.
- Adds inline control tags for emotions, gestures, scenes, and vocal delivery to drive real-time avatar animation.
- Enforces plain spoken dialogue (no markdown or stage directions).
- Provides detailed usage rules and tag reference for consistent in-character replies.
